subject: Hosted API: post-demo follow-up — monthly token runway & peak TPS
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
To: Ben Solo <ben.solo@skywaylabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 22:12:00 +0000
Subject: Hosted API: post-demo follow-up — monthly token runway & peak TPS

Ben — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and the few items we need to lock down so we can size a hosted pricing proposal:  

- Expected steady-state monthly token volume (range is fine): please give a conservative and an optimistic figure (e.g., 50M — 200M tokens / month).
- Peak TPS / concurrency profile: what’s your 99th percentile TPS during busy events and any expected burst windows?
- Token mix: rough split between generation (chat/completion) vs embeddings vs reranking (percentages are fine).
- Target unit economics: do you have an internal target $/1M tokens or an upper bound budget for the feature?
- Procurement / SOW constraints: any required billing terms, PO cadence, or security checklist items we should pre-seed into the SOW?

I attached the short traffic snapshot you shared on the call — pulled into a CSV so we can align numbers. If you can reply with the ranges above by EOD Tuesday (Mar 2) we’ll produce a ballpark hosted pricing sheet and a suggested SLA/burst plan.

Next steps we’ll take after your numbers:  
1) Run sensitivity across 3 slab options (monthly commit bands) + burst add-on.
2) Recommend a dollar-per-1M token headline and a 30/60/90 day trial conversion tie.
3) Draft a short SOW for procurement to review (no legal redline yet).

Thanks —
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0183

Attachments: skyway_traffic_snapshot_20260301.csv (CSV, 22 KB)

From: Ben Solo <ben.solo@skywaylabs.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Cc: Skyway Labs Procurement <procurement@skywaylabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API: post-demo follow-up — monthly token runway & peak TPS

Thanks Nikhil — good demo. Answers inline:  

- Steady-state monthly tokens (conservative -> optimistic): 35,000,000 -> 140,000,000 tokens/month. Most of this is customer-facing chat.
- Peak TPS: typical spikes are small but our Black Friday-like marketing pushes hit ~45 TPS sustained for 20–30 minutes; 99th percentile during normal ops is ~12 TPS. We’d expect 2–3 controlled bursts per quarter.
- Token mix: ~80% chat generation, ~15% embeddings (vector search), ~5% reranking/other.
- Target $/1M: we’re aiming for under $18 per 1M tokens ideally; can stretch to $22 for guaranteed latency/SLA.
- Procurement: we need net-45 invoicing and our standard security questionnaire (SOC 2 + data retention terms). Procurement is looped.

I attached our internal traffic extract (same as you have) — let me know if you want the raw event logs.

—Ben
Ben Solo
Head of Integrations, Skyway Labs
ben.solo@skywaylabs.com

On Mon, Mar 2, 2026 at 10:05 AM Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the time, Ben. Sending a short follow-up with asks.

Attachments: skyway_traffic_snapshot_20260301.csv (CSV, 22 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Solo <ben.solo@skywaylabs.com>, Skyway Labs Procurement <procurement@skywaylabs.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 18:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API: post-demo follow-up — monthly token runway & peak TPS

Ben / Procurement — appreciate the quick numbers. Two operational asks from our side before we scope a firm price:  

1) Can the procurement contact share any standard exceptions for net-45 (billing contact + PO flow)? We commonly do monthly consolidated invoices tied to the monthly commit.
2) For the SOC 2 + retention asks: please share the specific controls or a link to your security questionnaire so the security team can pre-fill answers and estimate any evidence turnaround.

Based on the token ranges Nikhil will model three slab options: 50M, 100M, 200M monthly commit equivalents (we’ll map your conservative/optimistic numbers). We’ll include a $/1M headline for each slab and a recommended burst add-on to cover the 45 TPS marketing spike. If the $/1M target is ~18–22 you should expect one of the middle slabs to align with that, subject to burst and SLA needs.

I’ll drop a first-draft pricing PDF tomorrow and a short SOW stub (no signature required).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments mentioned: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ben Solo <ben.solo@skywaylabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>, Skyway Labs Procurement <procurement@skywaylabs.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API: post-demo follow-up — monthly token runway & peak TPS

Ben — quick technical note from infra/ops side:  

- For a 45 TPS 20–30 minute burst we recommend: 1) a baseline slab sized to cover the 99th percentile (12 TPS) and 2) a burst buffer (auto-burst capacity) that covers up to +4x the 99th (so ~48 TPS) with a short warm-up window. That keeps steady costs lower while protecting high-impact events.
- We’ll propose a burst add-on as either a per-minute overage or a short-term reserved burst pool depending on your procurement preference.

I attached a very short example SOW/pricing stub we use for hosted customers (includes invoicing and PO line items). If Procurement can share any required vendor details (W-9, billing address, contact) we’ll include those in the draft.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Platform, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_hosted_pricing_v1.pdf (PDF, 34 KB); SOW_stub_example.docx (DOCX, 18 KB)
snippet: Post-demo recap asking for monthly token ranges, 99th TPS, token mix, and target $/1M — customer provided ranges and procurement requirements; ops recommends slab+burst approach.
